# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### gp3 read-bytes alarm in ALARM
**Description:** CloudWatch alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes (VolumeReadBytes Sum, 60s period, threshold 6.0E9) went to ALARM at 2026-11-23 16:23:18 UTC. The last 3 datapoints were ~7.87E9 bytes/min. Volume: vol-0123456789abcdef0, account 012345678901_1, us-east-1.
**Time:** 2026-11-23T16:20:00Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: gp3 volume capped at default 125 MiB/s throughput
**Description:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 (gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s, never modified; /dev/sdg on i-1234567890abcdef0_3) has served a read-only sequential workload of 256 KiB I/Os since 16:19 UTC on 2026-11-23. In every 1-minute sample from 16:20 to 16:48, reads sat at exactly 125.07 MiB/s while IOPS was only ~500 (17% of 3000). 500 IOPS x 256 KiB = 125 MiB/s, so the throughput limit binds long before the IOPS limit. Queue length rose to 1.5-1.7, idle time dropped to ~0 and per-read latency stayed ~3 ms: the volume is capping bandwidth, not slowing down per request. No config change or deployment was involved; the job's large-block reads simply hit the gp3 default throughput.
**Cascades to:** symptom-gp3-read-bytes-alarm

#### Supporting Observations
- **Volume is gp3 at baseline 3000 IOPS / 125 MiB/s:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 (example-b-gp3-throughput) is a 20 GiB gp3 volume with 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s provisioned throughput. It is attached to i-1234567890abcdef0_3 as /dev/sdg in us-east-1a and is unencrypted. The observed ~7.87E9 bytes/min works out to ~125 MiB/s, which matches the provisioned throughput ceiling.
- **Volume reads flat at ~125 MiB/s with 256 KiB I/O:** From 16:20 to 16:40 UTC, read throughput on vol-0123456789abcdef0 held at 125.07 MiB/s and ~500 read IOPS, with a constant 256 KiB I/O size and no writes. Queue length rose from 0 to ~1.5-1.7, idle time fell to ~0 s, and average read latency was ~3 ms. VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeIOPSExceededCheck returned no data. The volume has no modification history.
- **1-minute reads flat at 125.04-125.10 MiB/s:** At 1-minute resolution, reads ramped at 16:19 (66 MiB/s). From 16:20 to 16:48 they held between 125.04 and 125.10 MiB/s with no variance, the signature of a hard throughput cap.
- **Instance EBS bandwidth below c6i.xlarge baseline:** i-1234567890abcdef0_3 is a Nitro c6i.xlarge, EBS-optimized by default. Its baseline EBS throughput is 156.25 MB/s, with bursts to 1250 MB/s. Total instance EBS throughput was ~132.9 MiB/s from 16:20, made up of ~125 MiB/s from vol-0123456789abcdef0 and ~7.8 MiB/s from io2 vol-1234567890abcdef0_4. vol-1234567890abcdef0_15 was idle. InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck and InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck were 0 throughout 16:15-16:45. EBSByteBalance% and EBSIOBalance% stayed at 99% and CPU at ~1.2%, so the instance is not the bottleneck.

#### Gaps
- **VolumeThroughputExceededCheck returned no data:** The volume-level throughput-exceeded check for vol-0123456789abcdef0 had no datapoints, so the throttling conclusion rests on the flat plateau exactly matching the provisioned 125 MiB/s.
- **Guest-level I/O behavior not inspected:** Readahead and the number of requests the job keeps in flight inside i-1234567890abcdef0_3 were not examined, so it is not known how much throughput the job can actually use.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Raise the provisioned throughput of gp3 volume vol-0123456789abcdef0 (/dev/sdg on i-1234567890abcdef0_3) from 125 to 250 MiB/s with an online Elastic Volumes modification, keeping IOPS (3000) and size (20 GiB) unchanged. If the job needs more than ~141 MiB/s sustained, follow up by resizing the instance from c6i.xlarge to c6i.2xlarge in a maintenance window.

## Reasoning
Since 16:20 UTC, 256 KiB sequential reads have held the volume at exactly 125.07 MiB/s, the gp3 default cap. IOPS is ~17% used, so raising IOPS would not help. The volume has never been modified, so no cooldown applies, and at 3000 IOPS gp3 allows up to 750 MiB/s. The next ceiling is the c6i.xlarge baseline of 156.25 MB/s (~149 MiB/s), of which the io2 volume uses ~7.8 MiB/s, leaving ~141 MiB/s sustained. At 250 MiB/s the job can use the instance burst headroom (EBSByteBalance% is at 99%). Once credits run out it falls back to ~141 MiB/s, still ~13% better than today. A lasting gain needs c6i.2xlarge (312.5 MB/s baseline), which requires a stop/start.
